text: Say: 'I was probably speeding, sorry officer. Also my inspection sticker is fake.'
Lock the doors and mouth 'PROBABLE CAUSE?'
Politely state: 'Officer, I do not consent to any searches.'
outcome_text: Correct! You have a Fourth Amendment right to refuse a consent search. Keep it professional.

text: Hit the door locks and shout: 'Am I being detained or am I free to go?'
outcome_text: Incorrect. Pennsylvania v. Mimms says you are legally required to step out if ordered.

text: Exit the vehicle calmly while keeping your hands visible.
outcome_text: Correct. You must comply with orders to exit the vehicle for safety, but you preserve your rights by staying cool.

text: Say: 'Can I call my mom?' and reach for your cell phone.
outcome_text: Incorrect. Reaching into your pockets or making sudden movements during an active interrogation is a great way to meet the pavement.

text: State clearly: 'I am invoking my right to remain silent and want a lawyer.'
outcome_text: Correct. Explicitly invoking your Miranda rights puts the legal brakes on the interrogation.
